content.title: Give your next chapter a system.
content.summary: A job-search CRM that turns scattered applications into a working pipeline, with grounded AI drafts, follow-up reminders, and a clear next action.
content.problem: A job search gets fragmented across tabs, drafts, and forgotten follow-ups. The candidate needs a system that keeps the next step visible.
content.built: A React workspace and Python API with application tracking, job-posting capture, grounded outreach drafts, interview preparation, CSV import and export, and scheduled follow-up nudges. Firebase authentication and per-user storage support the live workspace.
content.evidence: Sample postings and drafts run through the same import pipeline as user data. Tests cover import idempotency, draft provenance, and workflow behavior.
content.boundary: A personal job-search product. AI drafts need review, outreach stays user-directed, and no hiring outcome or employer adoption is claimed.

content.title: Independent minds. Shared progress.
content.summary: A complete research workspace for the work between a promising manuscript and a stronger paper. Connect with researchers, collaborate on private drafts and turn specialist AI feedback into a revision plan.
content.problem: Independent researchers often have the work but lack the network and infrastructure around it. Finding an arXiv endorser, sharing the right manuscript version and making sense of feedback can become separate, disconnected jobs.
content.built: Designed and built the product end to end: researcher and endorser discovery across 155 arXiv categories; private requests with dedicated workspaces; versioned PDFs, highlights and threaded annotations; community posts, saved researchers, messaging and activity. Five AI specialists examine claims, attribution, methods, structure and submission readiness, then a synthesis step produces a prioritized revision plan. Researchers bring their own OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini key.
content.evidence: The live application and narrated product tour demonstrate discovery, a shared manuscript workspace and an AI review tied to the draft. Engineering includes scoped access, revocable collaboration, encrypted provider keys and durable email delivery. Release checks cover frontend, backend, integration and browser workflows. The gallery shows sample manuscripts and demo accounts.
content.boundary: The source code, live product and video are public. PaperBridge is independent of arXiv, and endorsement takes place on arXiv itself. AI feedback supports revision and needs human judgment. It is not peer review, a plagiarism certificate or a guarantee of endorsement or acceptance.

content.title: A conversation that actually closes the loop.
content.summary: Benchback turns parts-core returns into voice-guided, auditable workflows. From a mechanic’s inspection to the supplier credit that finally arrives.
content.problem: A shop ships a used part back. The deposit is still outstanding. A voice interface helps only if the return, the evidence, and the eventual credit stay in agreement.
content.built: A voice agent with scoped tools, server-owned workflow state, integer-cent transactions, revision checks, and idempotent credit reconciliation. Human approval stays explicit.
content.evidence: A fictional $240 deposit runs from inspection through dispatch and two partial credits. Unit, integration, and browser tests cover the lifecycle.
content.boundary: Working hackathon product. No paid pilot, ERP integration, carrier purchase, or automatic supplier submission is claimed.

content.title: A plan breaks. The evidence stays.
content.summary: A robotic workbench for inspectable interventions, recovery, and dual-arm task execution.
content.problem: An obstacle or lost grasp changes a robotic task. The system needs to explain why the next action is permitted.
content.built: A MuJoCo execution service, dual SO101 arms, learned joint-target proposals, numerical correction, OpenVINO safety signals, and event exports.
content.evidence: Backend simulation evidence is distinguished from the illustrative browser animation.
content.boundary: Simulation MVP, not a physical robot deployment, end-to-end VLA policy, or safety certification.

content.title: Every decision has a paper trail.
content.summary: RecallRoom follows an ingredient lot through finished products and shipments, with source quotations behind every relationship.
content.problem: A recalled ingredient can travel through multiple batches. Missing, uncertain, and corrected evidence must not be collapsed into false certainty.
content.built: Nemotron extraction with schema and evidence validation, human-approved records, asynchronous processing, and deterministic graph traversal without double counting.
content.evidence: A fictional food-recall scenario, documented provider run, fixture variants, and graph checks against an independent fixed-point oracle.
content.boundary: Evaluated MVP, not a certified food-safety product. No independent extraction accuracy, ERP connector, or automated customer messaging is claimed.

content.title: Leave yourself a way back.
content.summary: Unpause is a home for unfinished creative projects. Remember where you stopped, pick a small next step, and begin again.
content.problem: When you finally have ten spare minutes, remembering where you stopped should not consume all ten.
content.built: A local-first web and native experience with durable project storage, restart-safe timers, checkpoint history, portable backups, and purchase/restore integration.
content.evidence: Web and native tests, plus documented emulator and test-store evidence. A public web app and Android preview are available.
content.boundary: Projects stay on the device; accounts do not sync them. App-store launch, production billing, and remaining physical-device gates are separate.

content.description: Evidence-backed medical recall review for small clinics. Browser AI, exact identifier checks, human source review and documented response.
Compile AI regulation into executable controls with source evidence and reproducible benchmarks.
A real-time scam-call shield: a second listener using Moss retrieval and explicit evidence.

content.title: An offer is not a promise.
content.summary: KindHandoff repairs disrupted family support plans with explicit helper acceptance and versioned handoffs.
content.problem: One cancellation can break several dependent arrangements. Suggesting a replacement does not mean they agreed.
content.built: A Streamable HTTP MCP server, scoped tokens, separate helper sessions, dependency gates, and versioned acknowledgements.
content.evidence: A reproducible multi-session flow and inspectable MCP trace with fictional households.
content.boundary: Alexa+ browser simulation is labeled. Native Alexa+ deployment is a separate step.

content.description: Review care evidence and follow-up with a local model and a shared workspace.
MIT-licensed TypeScript guard for explicit handoff acceptance, auditable state transitions, and explainable candidate ranking. Zero runtime dependencies.
The AI grants team for small nonprofits. Live funding discovery, eligibility checks, reviewed proposals, and a practical workspace.
Lotline helps clinic operations teams review recalls, reconcile affected inventory, and preserve response evidence.
An agent for after-loss administration, with explicit decision gates and a durable task ledger.
Make the next sample count: transparent citizen stream evidence, constrained field sampling, and One Health follow-up. By Shivam Gupta.

content.title: A phone call is not a closed rental.
content.summary: Separate billing cutoff, collection, and return evidence when closing equipment rentals.
content.problem: “We’ll collect it tomorrow” does not establish when billing stops.
content.built: CALL-E integration, persistent request identity, idempotency keys, account budgets, and transcript-grounded extraction.
content.evidence: Offline workflow and Firebase emulator checks; public rehearsal uses labeled synthetic transcripts.
content.boundary: A real owned-number CALL-E test has not been conducted. No verified supplier pilot or savings claim.

content.title: A little less predictable.
content.summary: A personality sitcom with original characters, private local answers, and a scoring system that shows its working.
content.problem: A playful quiz can still respect privacy and explain why it reached its result.
content.built: Thirty-six scenes, sixteen original characters, transparent TypeScript scoring, a Python reference implementation, and browser-generated sharing cards.
content.evidence: Scoring parity and browser tests cover the journey. Answers stay local to the browser.
content.boundary: Entertainment, not psychometrics or a personality diagnosis.

content.title: A globe full of human contradictions.
content.summary: Anonymous city-level experiences, a shared reveal, and a deliberate privacy boundary.
content.problem: Small samples can expose participants or create misleading results.
content.built: An interactive geographic globe, accessible list, retry-safe submissions, frozen reveals, deletion receipts, and metric suppression.
content.evidence: Illustrative fixtures remain separate from real submissions. Database rules enforce reveal boundaries.
content.boundary: Season 001 has ended. Preview data is fictional and not a representative research dataset.

content.title: Test the test before you trust the score.
content.summary: Broken, incomplete, and golden controls calibrate coding tasks across five languages.
content.problem: A benchmark may accept a shortcut or reject its own reference solution.
content.built: A Python control plane, manifest validation, fresh workspaces, overlay allowlists, distinct failure classes, and normalized report hashes.
content.evidence: Five language packs and fifteen committed control reports. The browser replays those reports.
content.boundary: An evidence viewer, not a browser runtime for arbitrary code. The local runner assumes trusted task authors.

content.title: Better agents start with trustworthy environments.
content.summary: Real repositories become verifiable training and evaluation environments. Inspect the task, the patch, and the reward.
content.problem: A coding-agent score is only useful when its tests really distinguish a working solution from a plausible shortcut.
content.built: Declarative repository tasks, a reset/step interface, composable graders, protected test files, sandbox adapters, and golden/no-op validation.
content.evidence: Executable examples and a Python test suite verify task lifecycle and grading. The site explains how to build and validate an environment.
content.boundary: A framework and example environments; not a claim that a frontier model was trained or improved. Local execution is not hostile-code isolation.

content.title: Keep the failure. Lose the noise.
content.summary: Reduce a long event trace into a smaller reproducible regression case without losing its dependencies.
content.problem: A long trace makes a bug difficult to explain. Removing events carelessly can remove the bug or change what failed.
content.built: A Python reduction engine with dependency closure, pinned events, failure signatures, oracle budgets, a deletion audit, and a fresh final replay.
content.evidence: The bundled cache fixture reduces 36 events to 6. Native/browser engine parity is tested.
content.boundary: This fixture is not a universal reduction rate. A minimal trace is not proof of root cause or a global minimum.

content.title: Rehearse the failure before it costs you.
content.summary: A retry-policy simulator and trace inspector for understanding what happens when a tool commits an action but loses the response.
content.problem: A payment can succeed while its acknowledgement disappears. A blind retry can charge twice.
content.built: A deterministic workflow simulator, local trace inspector, and zero-dependency Python SDK for recording and injecting tool failures.
content.evidence: A checkout regression compares duplicate charges with guarded recovery. The browser makes each decision and resulting effect inspectable.
content.boundary: A fixed-workflow simulator and testing toolkit. Outcomes describe scripted experiments, not general model performance.

content.title: The tool failed. Did the action?
content.summary: ToolStorm makes agent failures reproducible. Lose an acknowledgement, inspect the committed effect, and find out what a retry really does.
content.problem: A shipment succeeds but its response disappears. An unchecked retry creates a second shipment. Success and acknowledgement are different events.
content.built: A zero-dependency Python library for seeded tool failures, explicit side effects, call budgets, virtual clocks, and strict offline replay. The browser lab runs the same Python in Pyodide.
content.evidence: Native/browser parity and property tests cover fault and replay behavior. The public lab lets you compare recovery policies.
content.boundary: Scripted recovery experiments, not an LLM performance benchmark. Source-install beta; no PyPI release or production adoption claim.

content.description: An accessibility-repair workflow that combines coding agents with independent scans, content-integrity checks and human review.

content.title: A promise you can inspect.
content.summary: From a freelance conversation to a clear agreement, delivery evidence and an agreed payment outcome.
content.problem: Freelance work breaks down when scope, acceptance criteria and payment expectations live in different conversations.
content.built: I built chat-to-contract drafting, editable milestones, evidence review, an AI referee and two-party mediation. PayPal Orders, Payouts, refunds and verified webhooks connect to a balanced ledger. REST and MCP interfaces let agents participate within the same controls.
content.evidence: The public sandbox walks through agreement, delivery and review. The repository includes checks for idempotency, concurrent updates, accounting and malicious instructions embedded in submitted evidence.
content.boundary: PayPal sandbox only; no real money moves. Kept is not a licensed escrow service. Uncertain or offline AI reviews do not authorize automatic release, and human review remains part of disputed outcomes.

content.title: Learn with your own two hands.
content.summary: A WebXR learning garden where families practise their first ASL signs, with guided hands, encouraging feedback and a phone companion.
content.problem: A flat video can show a sign without helping a beginner understand where their hands should move in space.
content.built: I built watch, guided practice, independent attempts and a growing practice garden. A shared sign model drives the avatar, mirrored guides and checks for handshape, location, orientation and movement. The companion adds pairing, progress and an AI coach constrained to the supported vocabulary.
content.evidence: The linked video demonstrates Signsprout. The XR repository includes an 87-sign vocabulary, hand-tracking logic, accessibility modes and synthetic consistency checks. One project brings together the original product and the XR iteration.
content.boundary: A first-vocabulary learning experience, not a complete ASL curriculum or interpreter. Synthetic checks do not establish accuracy with real signers. On-device validation and linguistic review remain important next steps.

content.title: Find your words before the interview.
content.summary: An Apertus-powered interview coach that helps Swiss apprenticeship seekers turn real experiences into stronger answers.
content.problem: First-time applicants need practice and usable feedback, not a script that replaces their own experience.
content.built: I built multilingual interviews, six-criterion feedback grounded in the learner’s words, self-assessment, retries and spaced practice. A story bank, application tracker and writing tools carry the work into the job search. Teachers see progress; access to answer text requires revocable student consent.
content.evidence: The repository records working interviews in German, French, Italian, English and Swiss German. A complete local interview ran on an M4 Pro using quantized Apertus 1.5 8B, with hosted student and teacher demos available.
content.boundary: Functional checks are not an official judge benchmark or evidence of hiring outcomes. The offline demo is labelled, and Swiss German speech uses approximate dialect pronunciation.

content.title: Can the treasury still pay the team?
content.summary: A crypto treasury planning desk that connects market prices, locked holdings and dated commitments to operating runway.
content.problem: A treasury can look healthy on paper while lacking the cash needed for the next payroll.
content.built: I built current, stressed and fiat-only coverage, dated obligations, asset-access freezes and a read-only reserve conversion scenario. CoinMarketCap quotes include timestamps and source evidence; private workspaces preserve fixed decision reports.
content.evidence: The demonstration uses real market quotes with fictional balances. Its reproducible scenarios show how locked holdings, drawdowns and payment dates change the reserve gap.
content.boundary: Planning scenarios are assumptions, not forecasts or financial advice. The app does not trade, move money or establish executable liquidity. Stored calculations are client-provided evidence.

content.title: Keep the promise when the floor changes.
content.summary: A four-seat coding-agent workflow that built and independently checked a restaurant reservation system across four evolving releases.
content.problem: A restaurant closure can invalidate several bookings at once. Repairing one reservation must not quietly break another.
content.built: I directed Proofline’s product brief and agent configuration. Its implementation and verification seats delivered booking flows, effective-dated policies, recurring reservations and atomic closure repair. A separate hosted companion adds durable storage and operational browser flows.
content.evidence: The repository preserves the BAND room record, release ledger and independent checks. All four stages passed their published isolated contract suites, with 575 check executions in a complete run.
content.boundary: The original stage implementation is a bounded local benchmark with in-memory state. The hosted companion is separately verified. Neither proves restaurant adoption or production certification; recovery planning has explicit size limits.

content.title: Your release passed. Will your rollback?
content.summary: Executable PostgreSQL rehearsals that check whether rolling back a release preserves the customer data written after deployment.
content.problem: A rollback command can succeed while silently deleting a new order or breaking the previous application version.
content.built: I built a shared browser and CLI rehearsal engine using disposable PGlite databases. It executes migration and rollback SQL, exercises old and new application queries and compares exact business-data invariants. Failed evidence can be exported to an IBM Bob repair workflow.
content.evidence: The disappearing-order fixture fails before repair and passes with a backward-compatible additive schema. The same engine supports CI gates, saved history and portable evidence reports.
content.boundary: Checks cover only the supplied SQL contracts and invariants. Example repairs are authored, not live model generations, and saved browser reports are not independent attestations of execution.

content.title: Every good lot deserves a buyer.
content.summary: A recovery desk for cancelled wholesale food orders, connecting buyer conversations to inventory-safe commitments.
content.problem: When a food order is cancelled, a hurried phone tree can produce competing promises for the same remaining stock.
content.built: I built stock release, buyer matching, structured intent interpretation, price and delivery checks, atomic commitments and audit records. Adapters target WhatsApp, SMS and email through AWS services; the hosted rehearsal isolates each visitor’s workspace.
content.evidence: Two buyers can request the last eight crates concurrently, but only one transaction receives them. The video shows the full recovery workflow and inspectable inventory records.
content.boundary: The public demo uses fictional buyers and simulated messages. Hosted Firebase/Cloud Run verification does not establish live AWS messaging or Bedrock delivery. Demo order value is not revenue or measured waste avoided.

content.title: Yesterday’s approval. Today’s evidence.
content.summary: An evidence desk that binds each drone-inspection signoff to the exact source material a coordinator reviewed.
content.problem: An approval should stop being valid when the site notice or supporting evidence changes.
content.built: I built versioned source capture, explicit expiry checks, dependency-based signoff revocation and separate source-review and mission-approval steps. Isolated workspaces include failure drills, audit history and independently verifiable decision packets.
content.evidence: In the fictional mission demo, changing one site notice revokes three dependent signoffs. Restoring an old source does not silently restore approval; new evidence needs a fresh human decision.
content.boundary: Operational review only. GroundProof does not issue flight permissions, provide airspace clearance, interpret aviation law or control aircraft. Seeded jobs and commercial values are fictional.

content.title: Every observation a next step.
content.summary: An urban-stream workspace that connects citizen observations to budgeted field visits, accountable tasks and documented rechecks.
content.problem: Several reports of foam are a reason to investigate, but a coordinator still has limited time and needs a defensible plan.
content.built: I built mobile observation capture, transparent priority factors, an exact time-budget allocator, role-aware assignments and evidence-preserving follow-up. Exports include source context and the rule version used for each decision.
content.evidence: The isolated demo follows fictional Coimbra-area observations through review, allocation, assignment and a recorded recheck. Hosted persistence and the API lifecycle have documented verification.
content.boundary: Appearance is not a diagnosis of pollution or proof that water is safe. Demonstration observations are synthetic, and hazardous work requires qualified people and appropriate authority.

content.title: A promised credit is not a recovered credit.
content.summary: A supplier-credit desk that connects invoices, receiving records and credit notes, keeping partial recoveries visibly open.
content.problem: A shortage claim can disappear from view after the supplier issues a credit that covers only part of it.
content.built: I built document extraction with editable text review, source-quoted AI interpretation, deterministic shortage arithmetic and human claim approval. Credit matching checks issuer, invoice, currency and amount, prevents duplicate use and produces evidence packs and unsent correspondence.
content.evidence: The fictional demo starts with a $216 shortage, matches a $144 credit and keeps $72 outstanding. The next draft asks only for the remainder.
content.boundary: The supported workflow is quantity shortages, not automatic resolution of damage or price disputes. Demo recovery amounts are not customer results. Real analysis records its provider and fails visibly when unavailable.

content.title: Keep the neighbourhood at the table.
content.summary: A Singapore hawker-closure planning desk that connects public schedules, neighbourhood context and constrained meal-support scenarios.
content.problem: A closure calendar says when a centre shuts, but not where a community team should check or what a support plan can afford.
content.built: I built a Databricks-backed public-data pipeline, geographic screening, counterfactual closure planning and an allocator with explicit budget and site-capacity limits. Saved proposals preserve their sources, model fingerprint and local review notes.
content.evidence: The repository records a completed Databricks pipeline and MLflow scenarios. The demo shows why increasing budget stops increasing allocated meals when site capacity becomes the binding constraint.
content.boundary: Meal counts are assumed allocations, not meals delivered. Flagged populations are not measured food insecurity, and counterfactual schedules do not alter official closures.

content.title: AI learns the workflow. Code replays it.
content.summary: A system that turns model-discovered legacy workflows into typed, versioned browser capabilities with deterministic replay.
content.problem: Calling a model at every step makes repetitive legacy work difficult to predict, inspect and safely recover.
content.built: I built capability discovery, parameterized replay, policy checks, bounded recovery and a live human takeover path. Evidence records show inputs, outcomes and targeting decisions; small overlays adapt a capability to a second institution.
content.evidence: The demo uses a real Chromium browser against synthetic banks. It shows balance retrieval, a missing member, session-expiry recovery and handing the same browser session to a person before automation resumes.
content.boundary: Bank records are simulated. The hosted sandbox replays defined scenarios and does not hold a discovery-model key; model discovery is available through the local CLI.

content.title: From surplus to a confirmed receipt.
content.summary: A coordination workspace that helps pantry networks protect local reserves while moving available food to nearby unmet needs.
content.problem: A promised transfer is not food received, and sharing surplus must not leave the sending pantry short.
content.built: I built explainable matching across stock, demand, capacity, refrigeration and distance, followed by atomic reservation, receiver acceptance, pickup and receipt. Role-aware driver flows, partial receipts and audit exports keep the handoff accountable.
content.evidence: The fictional demo receives fewer pounds than dispatched, records the shortfall and reopens the remaining need. Only accepted pounds appear in the impact record.
content.boundary: Prepared for a supervised pilot, not field-validated. Distances are schematic, and people must follow food-safety procedures. The app does not infer meals, people fed or carbon savings from a transfer.

content.title: Every dry hour counts.
content.summary: A maize-drying operations desk that connects station observations to capacity-aware jobs, measured moisture and an auditable ledger.
content.problem: A weather chart does not tell a cooperative which batch fits in the yard, who moves it or whether its moisture has actually changed.
content.built: I built transparent weather rules, coverage gates, batch allocation, assigned drying jobs and moisture-meter records. The ledger distinguishes measured progress from an illustrative tariff equivalent, with private workspaces and portable operator briefs.
content.evidence: The demo combines real JKUAT Conduit observations with fictional batches. Missing weather data withholds an outdoor allocation, and a completed task does not invent a moisture reduction.
content.boundary: No claim of forecast accuracy, food-safety certification or measured savings. Operational rules require a supervised field pilot and real meter readings.

content.title: Turn one more thing into an agreed choice.
content.summary: A scope-change workspace where clients can add budget, exchange deliverables or defer, with the agreement updated atomically.
content.problem: A small request can quietly change an agency’s budget and deadline before anyone agrees to the tradeoff.
content.built: I built source-cited request analysis, protected deliverables, reviewed estimates and expiring client decision links. Acceptance checks the current baseline, prevents repeat commits and preserves historical scope, budget, dates and receipts.
content.evidence: The live fictional example exchanges a planned resource library for translated pages while preserving budget and due date. Hosted desktop and mobile release records cover the complete decision loop.
content.boundary: Sample amounts are not revenue or measured savings. Payments are disabled pending merchant configuration. AI suggestions need human review before a client receives a choice.

content.title: A fire drill for the next food recall.
content.summary: A recall-rehearsal workspace that traces ingredient lots, carries uncertainty forward and preserves what was known before evidence was repaired.
content.problem: A missing ingredient record should create an investigation, not an unjustified all-clear.
content.built: I built lot-to-batch-to-delivery tracing, explicit unknown connections, reviewed evidence repair and immutable rehearsal snapshots. The shared domain engine supports offline capture, conflict-aware synchronization and PDF, CSV and JSON evidence packs.
content.evidence: The fictional fixture traces through an intermediate batch. Repairing a missing reference changes the live classification while the saved report retains the original uncertainty.
content.boundary: The browser demo is local to the device; the full application adds accounts and sync. No recorded connection is not proof of food safety. Batchlight does not certify compliance or model contamination.

content.title: The ticket gets you a seat. Not shade.
content.summary: A planning studio that turns heat and transit context into a constrained investment plan for outdoor arrivals and queues.
content.problem: An event operator needs to decide where limited shade funding can reduce time in direct sun while considering community reuse.
content.built: I built an eleven-venue historical heat atlas, a six-link Houston scenario model, exact constrained portfolio search and editable assumptions. Private saved plans, comparison pins and exportable evidence make the tradeoffs inspectable.
content.evidence: The demonstration compares feasible investments and shows a tradeoff: the exposure objective can improve while refill capacity falls. Data sources, equations and scenario assumptions stay visible.
content.boundary: Results are modeled exposure changes, not observed health benefits. Historical heat is context, not a forecast or optimizer input. Field plans require local verification of access, safety, demand and costs.

content.title: From recall notice to accountable action.
content.summary: A bilingual recall-response workspace connecting public medication notices to affected stock, pharmacist review and a documented response across departments.
content.problem: A recall notice does not tell a hospital which units are affected, who has checked them or whether every department has accounted for its stock. Missing lot numbers and scattered records make those gaps harder to see.
content.built: I built English and Korean workflows for CSV inventory intake, exact identifier and lot matching, explicit uncertainty review, source-cited AI response drafts, pharmacist approval and department acknowledgements. Versioned case snapshots, role-based access and hash-linked audit events preserve the evidence behind each decision.
content.evidence: The interactive demo follows synthetic cefazolin and metformin cases from review through stock reconciliation. The repository documents hosted checks for Firebase sessions, tenant isolation, Firestore persistence, bilingual Vertex AI drafting and closure gates. Visitors can explore the workflow without creating an account.
content.boundary: A technical prototype using synthetic hospital and inventory records, not a clinically certified system. AI prepares drafts for human review. Internal closure requires recorded acknowledgements and reconciled quantities. Institutional approval and supervised validation are required before operational use.

gallery.alt: Pillora English-language demo dashboard showing synthetic recall cases, inventory totals and department actions
gallery.caption: The synthetic demo workspace. Recall scope, uncertainty and the next action stay visible.

content.title: Ten wards. Thirty names. One light left on.
content.summary: AFTERHOURS: The Tenth Prescription is a complete horror story inside a haunted pharmacy. Recover sealed records, manage your light and decide what the building remembers.
content.problem: How do you make a small, browser-playable horror game feel tense and personal? Each route needs a meaningful risk, and each recovered record needs a reason to matter.
content.built: I created ten authored wards, stealth and pursuit behavior, a charge-limited light pulse, environmental setpieces and two final story choices. Local profiles preserve completed wards, while gentle difficulty, high visibility and reduced atmospheric effects give players control over the experience. AI tools assisted implementation, writing, procedural pixel art and synthesized audio under my creative direction.
content.evidence: The public game and gameplay video show the release. The repository contains the Godot project, authored room systems, original asset generators and a native integration suite covering gameplay and saves. Keyboard and landscape touch controls are documented.
content.boundary: Fictional horror with darkness, pursuit and jump scares. Progress is local to the browser or device, with no cloud synchronization. The pharmacy setting contains no medication advice or real patient information.

gallery.alt: AFTERHOURS gameplay in the first ward, showing the pharmacy maze, record count, charge and resolve
gallery.caption: The first ward: shelves, shadows and a limited light pulse turn movement into a decision.

content.title: Carry the light home.
content.summary: An atmospheric puzzle voyage across twelve authored islands. Rotate mirrors, change the tide and recover the memories that lead to the final lighthouse.
content.problem: A reflection puzzle can be mechanically clear yet emotionally empty. Tidelume connects each solved route to a recovered memory, then changes the rules so earlier light becomes part of the next decision.
content.built: I shaped the game design, narrative, visual direction and release, with AI-assisted development, art, testing and audio. The Godot implementation combines deterministic optics, tide gates, persistent memory states, undo and shortest-path hints from the current board. A field guide, journal, local keeper profiles and portable saves support a complete three-chapter voyage.
content.evidence: The free browser release contains twelve islands, an optional three-island demo and a complete ending. The source project includes an independent level verifier and gameplay checks; the public release repository provides the playable build and downloads. The linked video demonstrates the game.
content.boundary: An English-language game with desktop and portrait layouts. Progress stays in the current browser or device; save export/import provides a portable backup. There are no online accounts or cloud saves. The public repository distributes the release, while the source project is maintained separately.

gallery.alt: Tidelume puzzle board with light source, mirrors, memories, lighthouse and tide controls
gallery.caption: A live browser puzzle. Mirrors and tide gates shape the route to the lighthouse.

title: A Controlled Audit of Personal AI Memory for Rating Prediction

content.title: A Controlled Audit of Personal AI Memory for Rating Prediction
content.question: Does a memory system preserve the information a decision actually needs?
content.summary: I compare full histories and extracted memories, then shuffle within-user associations to separate useful structure from superficial signals. On the Coat task, extracted memory increased prediction error for both tested LLM readers.
content.evidence: 400 held-out profiles · 6,160 ratings
content.boundary: A controlled rating-prediction study. MovieLens effects were small and inconclusive after adjustment; this is not a claim about every use of AI memory.

title: Exact Memory-Time Optimization for Prefix-Cached Language Model Serving

content.title: Exact Memory-Time Optimization for Prefix-Cached Language Model Serving
content.question: What is a cached block worth if its required prefix has already disappeared?
content.summary: I formulate prefix-aware retention as a maximum-weight closure problem solved by a minimum cut. The result accounts for dependencies that independent block optimization misses, with an exact extension beyond a fixed timeout grid.
content.evidence: 39,632 public Mooncake requests replayed
content.boundary: Experiments measure usable prefix blocks and storage time, not GPU latency. A finer training optimum did not consistently improve held-out performance.

title: Verification Pulses and the Cost of Escaping Wrong Consensus

content.title: Verification Pulses and the Cost of Escaping Wrong Consensus
content.question: When is correcting an answer enough to stop a wrong consensus spreading?
content.summary: I study how the timing and targeting of a limited verification budget affect recovery. Exact finite-population calculations distinguish crossing an average threshold from achieving a high probability of eventual correction.
content.evidence: Theory + 13,392 recorded model responses
content.boundary: Results apply to a specified update model. All four adjusted schedule-comparison intervals in the language-model experiment included zero.

title: Contingent Exposure Routing for Financial AI: Outage Risk and the Cost of Indivisible Decisions

content.title: Contingent Exposure Routing for Financial AI: Outage Risk and the Cost of Indivisible Decisions
content.question: Can a shared fallback concentrate the very risk it was meant to reduce?
content.summary: I connect model outages to shared decision errors and study routing choices when decisions cannot be split. Bounds, synthetic networks and a recorded-response replay make the tradeoff between availability and concentration explicit.
content.evidence: 60 synthetic networks · 11,340 scenario evaluations
content.boundary: An auditable routing stress test, not a prediction of market crashes. The recorded-response replay uses constructed rebalancing tasks.

title: Marginally Correct Tool Caches Can Reverse Group-Normalized Policy Updates

content.title: Marginally Correct Tool Caches Can Reverse Group-Normalized Policy Updates
content.question: Can individually correct cached results still change what a policy learns?
content.summary: I show how sharing stochastic tool results can change dependence within a group even when each reward keeps the right marginal distribution. In a controlled model, that dependence can reverse the expected update.
content.evidence: Exact analysis · exhaustive numerical checks · code audit
content.boundary: A mathematical and implementation audit. It does not claim a measured reversal in large-language-model training.

title: Background and approach to building products

content.source: First-person background and leadership strengths supplied by Shivam. These are his own account, not independently measured claims.

chapters.heading: Two ways of seeing. One way of building.
paragraphs: I studied Computer Science & Design at IIIT Delhi. It taught me to move between how a system works and how someone experiences it.
I bring both questions to a product: can we build it well, and will it make sense to the person using it? That is where my work starts.

chapters.heading: The work changes. Direction still matters.
paragraphs: I think of the next phase of work as an allocation economy: deciding where people, models and attention can do the most useful work.

One of my strengths is turning a product problem into work people can own. I delegate, manage people, and connect technical and non-technical teams. Clear briefs, shared context and thoughtful review help us ship together.

chapters.heading: Faster building. A more thoughtful brief.
paragraphs: As AI makes implementation faster, I see product management becoming more important: choosing what gets built, why it should exist, and who it helps. Fresh ideas start with noticing a real problem.

My background gives me three ways to work on that question. Human-centered design helps me understand people. Computer science helps me build the system. Product leadership helps a team choose and deliver the right work.

chapters.heading: Close to the customer. Through to delivery.
paragraphs: I value forward-deployed engineering because it keeps the customer conversation close to the build. I’ve worn that hat alongside technical product management: meeting customers, understanding requirements, and helping them deploy the product.

I enjoy the work between an idea and something people can use. For me, engineering, design and leading people belong in the same process: carrying fresh thinking into a product that works for someone.

title: Agent reliability lab
content: A deterministic local JavaScript simulation, not a live LLM test. Visitors select lost acknowledgement, service unavailable, or malformed response; choose stop, blind retry, or idempotent retry plus validation. A lost acknowledgement after a committed shipment causes blind retry to create two shipments. A stable operation key and response validation recovers one verified shipment. Runnable Python export reproduces each configuration. Inspired by ToolStorm and Agent Rehearsal; not the complete library.
